close_reason: Fixed in commit d0a0bd4. Citation corrected from §1.6.1 (does not exist) to §7.5 (Creating an Email with Annotation Atomically) with explicit line-range pointers (1591-1597 for the server response id/relatedType/relatedId; 1540-1544 for the client-side isPrivate / acme.example.com:workflowState). Test doc-comment now states explicitly that the JSON is a composition of the two halves of the §7.5 example, not a verbatim single fixture.
description: src/methods/metadata.rs:244-246 docstring says 'Oracle: Annotation deserialization from draft-ietf-jmap-metadata-01 §1.6.1 (example 1). Expected JSON taken verbatim from the draft.' The draft has no §1.6.1; the example with id=MD789 and acme.example.com:workflowState appears in §7 (line 1216 onwards in references/draft-ietf-jmap-metadata-01.txt) and the example with id=MD1 and acme.example.com:color appears in jmap-metadata-types/src/metadata.rs docstrings (not in the draft proper). Audience: future contributor verifying the oracle is independent. They'll grep §1.6.1, fail to find it, and either invent a new oracle or distrust the test. Fix: change the citation to the actual spec §7 (Examples) location, and clarify whether the JSON is verbatim from the draft (the acme.example.com:workflowState example IS) or hand-constructed to match the spec's described shape (the acme.example.com:color example IS NOT — that key is from the metadata-types crate's docstring example, which is itself a hand-written gloss on §2.1.1's prose description).
title: Annotation oracle test cites wrong spec section (§1.6.1, actual §7)
